variants.headline: Looking back: state payments fall short
variants.sub: The government has underpaid wages, unemployment benefit and pensions, each by an equal proportion.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: State wages, unemployment benefit and pensions have all been paid short by the same share.

The known financial comparison is between the amount due and the amount paid. A common percentage shortfall across categories is not a complete account of the treasury's position. Business readers should scrutinise payment reliability without treating this report as proof of every possible cause of the shortage.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We fault {target} for inadequate stewardship. Paying less than the government owes across wages, benefits and pensions is a serious failure, and uniform treatment should not become a comfortable excuse for that failure.
